## Stakes (Extrapolating) {#intro}

Official unit for 2026–2027: **INT_52402_EP — 16-week research-oriented internship (academic or in a public/private company)**, listed in LLGA 1 – S2 and taught in period 3; 20 ECTS per the LLGA wiki. The rest of this page is our own framing. The M1 research internship is the first major test outside the classroom: state a question, read the literature, experiment, and report. Empirically, this is where the Graph×LLM track becomes a *topic* rather than a pile of modules.

It is not yet the end-of-studies internship (24 ECTS in M2): the accent is research-oriented — academic lab, industrial R&D, or hybrids — with a report / poster / reproducible code deliverable depending on supervision.

## Place in the 2-year path {#place}

**Upstream**: P1–P2. **Here**: P3 immersion. **Downstream**: M2 specialization then [end-of-studies internship](../m2-internship/index.html). Many M2 topics read better after touching one paper end-to-end in M1.

See [After the master](../../index.html#checkpoints) on the home page for the roles and problem spaces the track opens onto; they help when choosing the direction of a topic.

### From your Year 1 project to an internship proposal {#from-project}

The Year 1 [end-of-year projects](../../projects/index.html) are a dress rehearsal for this internship. They run until about two weeks after the end of Period 2, before it starts, and they follow the rules of this page: one question, one metric and one baseline per work package, a weekly log, at least 3 seeds and a reproducible repository. Their last deliverable is a one-page open question for the research internship ([deliverables](../../projects/index.html#deliverables)). That page is the seed of your topic.

Turn it into a two-page proposal before the internship begins. Reuse the project's open question, its metric and its retrained baseline, so that the internship starts from a number you already trust. Then state three things: the gain you expect over the project result, what the host brings (data, compute, expertise), and the Year 1 chapters the work relies on. The host will reshape the question; the proposal still shows that you can scope one.

Each project prepares a family of internship topics, which a Year 2 [Transverse project](../m2-projet-transverse/index.html) can then continue. The table repeats the [continuation table](../../projects/index.html#glance-continuation) of the projects page.

| Year 1 project | Internship topic family it prepares | Year 2 project |
|---|---|---|
| [Y1.1](../../projects/index.html#y1-1) KG-QA router | relation extraction, KG quality, retrieval evaluation | [Y2.1](../../projects/index.html#y2-1) |
| [Y1.2](../../projects/index.html#y1-2) fleet dispatch | spatio-temporal forecasting, RL for operations | [Y2.4](../../projects/index.html#y2-4) |
| [Y1.3](../../projects/index.html#y1-3) news recommendation | recommender systems, bandits, privacy or fairness | [Y2.3](../../projects/index.html#y2-3), [Y2.5](../../projects/index.html#y2-5) |
| [Y1.4](../../projects/index.html#y1-4) molecules from words | molecular ML, generative chemistry | [Y2.2](../../projects/index.html#y2-2) |
| [Y1.5](../../projects/index.html#y1-5) scene-graph QA | perception, neuro-symbolic reasoning, efficient inference | [Y2.3](../../projects/index.html#y2-3) |

## Industry and research links {#industrie}

**Research**: experimental method, baselines, ablations, writing. **Industry R&D**: the same [evidence bar](#travailler) with data/prod constraints. Helps choose for M2: doctoral research, ML engineering, or CIFRE frontier.

## How to approach it {#travailler}

-   One question, one metric, one baseline — before stacking models.
-   Weekly log: hypothesis → trial → result → next question.
-   Keep an explicit link to at least one Year 1 course you took, for example [Graph ML ch. 10](../m1p2-graph-ml/index.html#ch10) (GraphRAG and the hybrid), [Text Mining & NLP ch. 7](../m1p2-nlp-text-mining/index.html#ch7) (transformers, a minimal RAG pipeline), [Reinforcement Learning](../m1p2-reinforcement-learning/index.html), [Multimodal Generative AI](../m1p2-multimodal-genai/index.html) or [Optimal Transport](../m1p2-optimal-transport/index.html). The [Large Language Models](../m2-large-language-models/index.html) course comes later, in Year 2, Period 1.
-   Evidence bar: retrain the baseline in your own pipeline, use at least 3 seeds, compare with a paired test, ablate each new component and touch the test set once. This is the protocol of [Machine Learning 4.9](../m1p1-machine-learning/index.html#model-comparison); the [shared evaluation kit](../../projects/index.html#kit) of the end-of-year projects gathers the other tools.

### A 16-week milestone template {#milestones}

The template below is a proposal of these notes. Adapt it to the host's calendar; the supervisor sets the real milestones.

| Weeks | Milestone | Evidence at the end |
|---|---|---|
| W1–2 | Two-page proposal (question, metric, baseline, course anchor) and a literature map of 8–10 annotated papers | proposal agreed with the supervisor |
| W3–4 | Baseline reproduced in your own pipeline, on the host's data or a public proxy | baseline number within the reported variance, or the gap explained |
| W5–10 | Experiments, one hypothesis at a time, recorded in the weekly log | log entries and a results table over seeds |
| W11–12 | Ablations: remove each new component in turn | ablation table with standard deviations |
| W13–14 | Writing: full draft, figures regenerated by scripts | draft sent to the supervisor |
| W15–16 | Poster or defence, repository freeze | tagged release, poster or slides |

### Reproducibility checklist {#repro-checklist}

-   **Seeds**: at least 3 per trained model, reported as mean and standard deviation; seeding as in [Deep Learning 8.4](../m1p1-deep-learning/index.html#ch8).
-   **Configs**: every run starts from a versioned configuration file, saved with the commit hash next to its result.
-   **Lockfile**: exact package versions (`uv.lock` or a pinned requirements file) and, when possible, a Dockerfile, as in the repository template of the [CS refresher, 3.9](../m1p1-refresher-cs/index.html#ch3).
-   **Data versions**: a hash or a dated snapshot of each dataset, and the script that builds the splits.
-   **One command**: each reported number is regenerated from the README with one command, and a peer has tried it.

### Report skeleton {#report}

1.  **Abstract**: the question and the answer, with the headline number and its spread.
2.  **Introduction**: why the question matters, and the contributions in two or three bullets.
3.  **Related work**: the literature map, condensed to the papers you build on or compare with.
4.  **Method**: what is new, with the baseline it extends.
5.  **Experimental setup**: data and its version, splits, metric, baseline, seeds, compute budget.
6.  **Results**: mean and standard deviation over seeds, paired tests against the baseline.
7.  **Ablations and failure analysis**: what each component brings, and where the method fails.
8.  **Conclusion and open question**: what is settled, and the next question, which can seed the Year 2 work.
9.  **Appendix**: the commands, configurations and data hashes behind each number.

[Extrapolating]{.tag} Framing; internship rules and grading = programme / host lab.
